newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: One body recovered in Australia ski resort landslide.
newsitem.headline: One body recovered in Australia ski resort landslide.

text.p: One body has been found in the wreckage of two Australian ski lodges destroyed by a landslide which buried up to 20 people, police said on Thursday.

Police had earlier said that rescuers using optic fibre cameras and thermal imaging had found no signs of life in the ruins of the Thredbo Alpine Village in the Snowy Mountains, 400km (250 miles) south of Sydney.
"Fairly recently we have found one body," regional police commander Bruce Johnston told reporters, as rescuers continued searching under arc lights for survivors in the freezing night.
Police said the body was still in the ruins of the ski lodges and that they could not identify it.
The landslide occurred just before midnight on Wednesday at a time when Thredbo, at an altitude of 1,370 metres (4,500 feet), was packed with thousands of Australian and foreign visitors.
Tonnes of soil, rocks and gum trees crushed the Carinya lodge, which contained one person, sending it cascading onto the Bimbadeen lodge, which contained up to 19 people.
